groups.canonical_citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.63
groups.conflict_note: Official ordinance text does not state a specific effective date beyond the Council vote (Nov 18, 2025); a secondary source states an effective date of January 2026.
groups.interaction: This local ban operates alongside the state Cartwright Act's broader ban on coordinated pricing algorithms (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §16729), adding housing-specific penalties and private rights of action.

groups.canonical_citation: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.106 (Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance)
groups.interaction: Operates alongside state FEHA/Civil Rights Council criminal-history restrictions (Cal. Gov. Code §12955 and implementing regulations), providing additional local protections.

groups.canonical_citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76 (Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB)
groups.conflict_note: Measure BB's just-cause amendments were approved by voters in Nov. 2024 but no single provision effective date is given; relocation assistance amounts adjust annually (e.g., $19,413 effective 2026-01-01).
groups.interaction: Operates alongside the state Tenant Protection Act (Civ. Code §1946.2); because this local ordinance predates Sept. 1, 2019 (as amended), the state just-cause law yields to it for covered units.

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 (Tenant Protection Act of 2019)
groups.conflict_note: Section became operative April 1, 2024 as amended; a further amendment (AB 1529, Stats. 2025 Ch. 203) is effective Jan. 1, 2026, and the section is set to self-repeal Jan. 1, 2030; the original Tenant Protection Act took effect Jan. 1, 2020.
groups.interaction: State just-cause requirement does not apply where a qualifying local just-cause ordinance (adopted on or before Sept. 1, 2019, or a more protective local ordinance adopted later) governs the tenancy instead.

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 (Tenant Protection Act / AB 1482)
groups.conflict_note: Section operative April 1, 2024; repealed as of Jan. 1, 2030 absent further extension.
groups.interaction: State rent cap does not apply to units already covered by a qualifying local rent control ordinance (e.g., Berkeley, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Santa Ana).

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5
groups.conflict_note: Base one-month deposit cap (with 2-month exception for qualifying small landlords) effective July 1, 2024 (AB 12); a later amendment (AB 414) added itemization/nonrefundable-deposit provisions effective Jan. 1, 2026.

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6
groups.conflict_note: Base $30 cap (1998) is CPI-adjusted annually; current adjusted cap is $68.96 for 2026.

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (FEHA, as amended by SB 329 and SB 267)
groups.conflict_note: SB 329 (eff. Jan. 1, 2020) added source-of-income protections; SB 267 (2023) added a credit-history alternative-proof requirement for voucher holders; precise SB 267 effective date not specified in sources.

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 2 (Civil Rights Council criminal-history regulations implementing Cal. Gov. Code § 12955)
groups.conflict_note: One source cites only general FEHA authority without a specific regulatory section; citation harmonized to the Civil Rights Council's implementing regulations.

groups.canonical_citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (Cartwright Act, as amended by AB 325)
groups.conflict_note: No explicit effective date is stated in the statutory text itself; a secondary source corroborates a Jan. 1, 2026 effective date, consistent with standard California bill effective-date rules.
groups.interaction: This general antitrust prohibition applies statewide alongside housing-specific local algorithmic-pricing bans (Berkeley, San Francisco, San Diego, Santa Ana), which add housing-specific penalties and private enforcement rights.

groups.canonical_citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB)
groups.conflict_note: Measure BB's 5% Annual General Adjustment cap was approved by voters in Nov. 2024 without a clearly stated provision effective date; the 2026 AGA Order (1.0% increase), adopted Oct. 16, 2025, applies the cap's formula effective Jan. 1, 2026.
groups.interaction: Berkeley's local rent cap applies instead of the state AB 1482 cap for covered units; the state cap yields to this pre-existing local rent control ordinance under Civ. Code §1947.12(a)(2)(A).

groups.canonical_citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance - security deposit interest)
groups.interaction: Supplements the statewide security deposit cap (Civ. Code §1950.5) with a local interest-on-deposit requirement not found in state law.

groups.canonical_citation: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78
groups.interaction: Implements disclosure requirements tied to the state screening-fee cap (Cal. Civ. Code §1950.6) and adds a local prohibition on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies not found in state law.

groups.canonical_citation: L.A.M.C. § 151.09 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance)
groups.conflict_note: Relocation assistance amounts are adjusted annually (e.g., $11,000-$27,400 for the 2026-2027 period) and must be the higher of RSO/JCO amounts or state Housing Crisis Act amounts where applicable.
groups.interaction: Operates alongside the state Tenant Protection Act (Civ. Code §1946.2), which generally yields to this pre-existing local ordinance; also interacts with the state Housing Crisis Act's relocation requirements, with landlords owing whichever amount is higher.

groups.canonical_citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
groups.interaction: Covers units not subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance; together with the RSO's just-cause provisions it provides citywide just-cause coverage.

groups.canonical_citation: L.A.M.C. (Resident Protections Ordinance, Ord. Nos. 188481 & 188482)
groups.conflict_note: Enhanced relocation requirements must be reconciled with the state Housing Crisis Act; landlords must pay whichever amount (state or city) is higher for lower-income displaced tenants.
groups.interaction: Supplements RSO/JCO relocation requirements specifically for demolition of protected units for new construction, and interacts with the state Housing Crisis Act's relocation mandates.

groups.canonical_citation: L.A.M.C. § 151.06 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance)
groups.conflict_note: Allowable annual rent increase percentage is set each year (currently 3% for July 2025-June 2026); separate RSO and SCEP surcharges apply on top of the base increase.
groups.interaction: Applies instead of the state AB 1482 rent cap for RSO-covered units, which are exempt as already subject to a local rent control ordinance.
Supplements the statewide security deposit cap (Civ. Code §1950.5) with a local interest-payment requirement for RSO-covered units.
Operates alongside the state FEHA source-of-income protection (Cal. Gov. Code §12955), providing additional local enforcement.

groups.canonical_citation: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7 (§§ 98.0700-98.0707)
groups.conflict_note: Section 98.0706 was amended effective 3-28-2024 regarding relocation assistance; some SDHC portal notice requirements referenced in secondary sources are described as not yet in effect.
groups.interaction: Operates alongside California's statewide just-cause law (Civ. Code §1946.2); the local ordinance is designed to be consistent with and layered on top of state law, adding relocation assistance and stricter local protections.

groups.canonical_citation: San Diego Mun. Code § 98.1103
groups.conflict_note: An earlier staff report/draft of this same ordinance described it as pending with a blank final-passage date; it has since been enacted and codified at §98.1103.
groups.interaction: Operates alongside the state Cartwright Act's ban on common pricing algorithms (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §16729), providing housing-specific penalties and private enforcement rights.

groups.canonical_citation: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9
groups.conflict_note: Relocation payment amounts adjust annually (e.g., $8,245/tenant for owner-move-in/demolition evictions and $11,110.05/tenant for Ellis Act evictions, effective 3/01/26-2/28/27); relocation for temporary displacements under 20 days is instead governed by state law (Cal. Civ. Code §1947.9) rather than the local ordinance.
groups.interaction: Operates alongside California's statewide just-cause law (Civ. Code §1946.2), which yields to this pre-2019 local ordinance; relocation for brief (<20 day) displacements is instead governed directly by state law.

groups.canonical_citation: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.3
groups.conflict_note: Allowable increase rate is set annually (1.6% for 3/1/26-2/28/27; previously 1.4%).
groups.interaction: Applies instead of the state AB 1482 rent cap for units already covered by this local rent control ordinance.

groups.canonical_citation: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C
groups.interaction: Operates alongside the state Cartwright Act's ban on common pricing algorithms (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §16729).

groups.canonical_citation: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9 (security deposit interest)
groups.interaction: Supplements the statewide security deposit cap (Civ. Code §1950.5) with a local interest-payment requirement.

groups.canonical_citation: Santa Ana Mun. Code, Rent Stabilization Ordinance
groups.conflict_note: Current allowable increase rate is adjusted periodically (e.g., 2.87% for Sept. 2026-Aug. 2027).
groups.interaction: Applies instead of the state AB 1482 rent cap for units already covered by this local rent control ordinance.

groups.canonical_citation: Santa Ana Mun. Code, Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
groups.interaction: Operates alongside the state Tenant Protection Act (Civ. Code §1946.2); as this local ordinance was adopted after Sept. 1, 2019, its precise preemption interaction with state law is not fully clear from available sources.

groups.canonical_citation: Santa Ana Ordinance (Algorithmic Rent-Setting Software Ban)
groups.conflict_note: Sources disagree on enactment status: one describes the ordinance as pending a final vote scheduled March 3, 2026 after passing first reading Feb. 17, 2026; another describes it as already in effect. Treated as enacted on the assumption the scheduled final vote occurred.
groups.interaction: Operates alongside the state Cartwright Act's ban on common pricing algorithms (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §16729).
